outputs.tolerance: absolute 0.01 across seeds; deterministic at seed=11

known_limitations: Steady-state, well-mixed two-compartment series-conductance model with three independent log-uniform conductances (Q, E, K). It tests SUFFICIENCY: that a physiologically plausible vascular-egress or interstitial-exchange bottleneck is enough to drop the influx<->clearance Spearman correlation below 0.3 while preserving the neutral Pe substrate. It does NOT establish that real in vivo glymphatic transport lives in a bottleneck regime: the true physiological ranges and covariances of Q, E and K in vivo are unknown; covariation (e.g. Q and E rising together with pressure) could restore coupling; transient/accumulation effects are not modelled; and the perivenous PVS-efflux pathway that breaks the conservation-of-mass argument is represented only structurally, not calibrated to data. No real BOLD/tracer imaging data were used.
